metadata.name: movex_equities
metadata.description: Daily volatility markets on US stocks

instructions.name: claim
docs: Collects a winning share, or a refund from a voided market.

accounts.name: market
docs: Not mutable. The pools stay as the record of what was deposited, so a
claim never rewrites the denominator other claimants are dividing by.

accounts.name: position
docs: Seeds bind this to `user`, who signs, so no other position is
reachable from here.

instructions.name: claim_for_owner
docs: Pays a resolved position to its owner's token account. Anyone may
call it: the destination is derived from the owner, so nothing can
be sent anywhere else.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays for the owner's token account if it does not exist yet.

accounts.name: owner
docs: position and to derive the token account the payout goes to.

instructions.name: collect_fee
docs: Pushes a settled market's protocol fee to its treasury.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone may push the fee to the treasury. It can only go to the
address the market was created with, so there is nothing to gain by
calling it and no reason to gate it.

instructions.name: deposit
docs: Deposits into ABOVE or BELOW. Before lock at full weight; after lock,
where the market allows it, under a cap that decays to the deposit
less the fee at settlement.

accounts.name: position
docs: One per user, market and side. The side is in the address, so a user
holding both sides holds two of these and neither can touch the other.

instructions.name: faucet_mint
docs: Mints one allowance of the test token, subject to the cooldown.

accounts.name: claim
docs: Per-user, so one wallet draining the faucet does not affect anyone
else's cooldown.

instructions.name: init_faucet
docs: Opens a test-token faucet. Compiled out without `devnet-faucet`.

accounts.name: mint
docs: The faucet PDA must already hold mint authority, which is what makes
`faucet_mint` the only path to new supply. Anchor checks it here
rather than trusting the deployer to have wired it correctly.

instructions.name: init_market
docs: Creates a market with a frozen strike and its own vault.
The strike is not taken on trust. The instruction recomputes the
percentile from the sample series it was given and rejects the market
unless the two agree.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Holds every deposit for this market. Its authority is the market PDA,
so nothing can move funds except this program.

accounts.name: pyth_feed
docs: read here; validated when `lock` and `settle` actually consume it.

instructions.name: init_price_feed
docs: Opens a keeper-published price feed for one underlying.
Compiled out without `keeper-oracle`: a mainnet build reads Pyth and
has no instruction capable of writing a price at all.

instructions.name: lock
docs: Records the reference price and closes withdrawals. Permissionless.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Pays the fee. Anyone at all.

accounts.name: price_feed
docs: feed this market was created with so a crank cannot substitute one.

instructions.name: settle
docs: Records the settlement price and picks a side, or voids a market
whose losing side is empty. Permissionless.

accounts.name: price_feed
docs: feed this market was created with.

instructions.name: update_price
docs: Publishes a price. Only the feed's publisher may call it.

accounts.name: publisher
docs: Constrained to the publisher the feed was created with, so a feed
cannot be hijacked by whoever calls first.

instructions.name: void_market
docs: Releases a market that never resolved. Permissionless, and only after
the grace period.

instructions.name: withdraw
docs: Pulls a deposit back out. Only before lock.

accounts.name: position
docs: The seeds already bind this to `user`, who signs, so no separate
ownership constraint is needed: no other user's position can be
passed here at all.

types.name: Faucet
docs: Configuration for a self-serve test-token faucet.
The PDA itself is the mint authority, so the only way to create supply is
through `faucet_mint` and its cooldown. Gated on `devnet-faucet`: a
production build has no instruction that can mint the quote asset.

types.name: FaucetClaim
docs: One user's claim history against one faucet.

fields.name: underlying
docs: Ticker as ASCII, right-padded with spaces. `b"NVDA    "`.

fields.name: session_date
docs: `YYYY-MM-DD` of the session whose close becomes the reference price.

fields.name: samples_bps
docs: The 20 close-to-close moves the strike was read from, sorted ascending.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Wallet entitled to the fee on this market.

fields.name: live_deposits
docs: Whether deposits stay open after lock, under the cap below.

fields.name: live_max_multiple_bps
docs: The most a live deposit may be paid, in basis points of itself, for
one landing the instant the market locks. 20_000 is twice the deposit.

fields.name: live_cap_exp
docs: How fast that maximum decays across the window. 0 flat, 1 linear,
up to `MAX_LIVE_CAP_EXP`.

fields.name: live_cutoff_secs
docs: Live deposits close this many seconds before settlement.

types.name: LiveTotals
docs: Deposits that arrived after lock, reduced to the three integers the
payout needs. Kept on the market per side, and on each position for its
own share, accumulated with exactly the same terms so that every division
at claim time is by a sum of what it distributes.
`floor` is the least this money is paid back if its side wins, the
deposits less the fee. `excess` is how much more its cap allows, which is
what decays with the time left when each deposit landed.

fields.name: authority
docs: Allowed to create the market. Settlement is permissionless.

fields.name: underlying
docs: Ticker as ASCII, right-padded with spaces. Part of the PDA seeds.

fields.name: session_date
docs: `YYYY-MM-DD` of the session whose close is the reference price.

fields.name: pyth_feed
docs: Pyth price account this market settles against.

fields.name: quote_mint
docs: SPL mint deposits are denominated in (USDC).

fields.name: strike_bps
docs: The threshold, in basis points. 155 = 1.55%.
Not taken on trust: `init_market` recomputes the percentile from
`samples_bps` and rejects the market unless they agree. The strike is
enforced by the program, not merely asserted by the keeper.

fields.name: samples_bps
docs: The 20 absolute close-to-close moves the strike was read from, in
basis points, sorted ascending.
These are the public justification for the threshold. Holding them on
chain is the difference between "trust our API" and "here are the
twenty numbers, and the program checked them itself".

fields.name: reference_price
docs: Written at lock. Zero until then.

fields.name: settlement_price
docs: Written at settle. Zero until then.

fields.name: above_pool
docs: Everything deposited on each side, before and after lock.

fields.name: live_above
docs: The part of each pool that arrived after lock, with its cap.

fields.name: winning_side
docs: Written at settle.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Wallet entitled to the protocol fee. The destination token account
must be owned by it, so the fee has a declared home from the moment
the market is created rather than being decided later.

fields.name: fee_collected
docs: The fee is a single withdrawal, not a running balance.

fields.name: lock_ts
docs: Withdrawals close at this time and the reference price is taken.

fields.name: settle_ts
docs: The settlement price is taken at this time.

fields.name: live_deposits
docs: Whether deposits stay open after lock. The switch for the whole live
round: off, and the market behaves exactly as one without it.

fields.name: live_max_multiple_bps
docs: The most a live deposit may be paid, in basis points of itself, for
one landing the instant the market locks. Decays from there.

fields.name: live_cap_exp
docs: How fast that maximum decays over the window. Zero is flat.

fields.name: live_cutoff_secs
docs: Live deposits close this many seconds before settlement, so nothing
can be placed knowing the print the market will settle on.

fields.name: side
docs: Which pool this position sits in. The side is part of the account's
address, so one user may hold one position per side of a market and
the two never mix.

fields.name: amount
docs: Everything deposited, before and after lock.

fields.name: live
docs: The part of `amount` that arrived after lock, with its cap.

types.name: PriceFeed
docs: A price published by our own keeper.
Deliberately shaped like a Pyth sponsored feed: one fixed address per
underlying, updated continuously, read by both the program and the UI.
That is not imitation for its own sake. It means swapping to Pyth on
mainnet changes one file rather than the shape of everything above it.
What it lacks compared to Pyth is not structure, it is publishers. There
is exactly one and it is us, which is stated plainly in the README rather
than papered over. It exists because Pyth moved Hermes behind a $500/month
key in August 2026, which is outside a hackathon budget.
Compiled out entirely without `keeper-oracle`, so a production build has
no such account type and no instruction that writes one.

fields.name: publisher
docs: The only key allowed to write prices here.

fields.name: price
docs: Scaled by `KEEPER_PRICE_EXPONENT`.

fields.name: conf
docs: Spread across the sources that agreed on it, same scale.
The analogue of Pyth's confidence interval, and consumed by exactly
the same check: a wide band means the sources disagree and the market
refuses to settle rather than picking a number out of the spread.

fields.name: publish_time
docs: When the *source* produced this price, not when it was written here.
The distinction is the whole staleness check. A price written a second
ago carrying Friday's close is stale, and must read as stale.

fields.name: posted_slot
docs: Slot of the write. Only for diagnosing publisher lag.

fields.name: source_count
docs: How many independent sources agreed on this price.
